record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; paper source, PDF, and result files were not read. No text is reported as garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a refusal-related outcome after practical abliteration, a weight-edit approach, but does not say it applies the original activation-difference measurement and projection intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports one refusal-related result: Zephyr-7B-beta achieved 98% ASR after abliteration. The README does not identify which tool or give the evaluation setup or a pre-edit ASR. Tool compatibility counts and benchmark capability averages are not separate refusal results. The listed result files and figures were not read, so their contents are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study applies four released abliteration tools, which are weight-edit implementations of direction ablation, to 16 released instruct models. It reports refusal suppression (ASR), so its results bear on V2. Only the README was available. It gives one refusal number: Zephyr-7B-beta at 98% ASR.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that capability preservation varies by tool: ErisForge and DECCP degrade least, and GSM8K is the most sensitive benchmark. They say DPO-only alignment (Zephyr, 98% ASR, KL 0.076) is most susceptible, and that tool compatibility varies widely.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a comparative evaluation of four abliteration tools, not the original difference-in-means activation intervention. This is a tool/comparison repository; its reported result is a practical weight-edit outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says outcomes vary by tool and model; it reports the Zephyr result but does not state its tool or evaluation conditions.
record.problems: The refusal result has no stated pre-edit baseline, tool attribution, prompt set, judge, or uncertainty. The README's capability figures are aggregate tool-level GSM8K changes, not linked to the Zephyr refusal result or a particular tool/model condition. Listed result files and figures were not read.
record.rows_left_out: No other README results were extracted as rows: tool compatibility counts do not report the claim's behavior, and the GSM8K averages report capability changes without a linked refusal outcome or a test of V1's direction intervention. The README lists result JSON files and figures, but their contents are unavailable in the provided text.

untested.parts: Per-model and per-tool refusal rates for the 15 other models, and pre-edit baselines, are not in the README.
No direction measured, ablated or added at the activation level.
The alignment-method comment ('DPO-only most susceptible') does not test whether one removable direction exists.
Not tested. Qwen3 models are included, but no reasoning-mode result is reported.

missing.what: Per-model and per-tool refusal/ASR results, before and after abliteration, for all 16 models. These are needed to see where V2 fails (the README calls Zephyr 'most susceptible', implying lower ASR elsewhere).
Capability cost of the weight edit by tool and model (GSM8K change from +1.51 to -18.81 pp). This bears on whether practical removal keeps other abilities.

Tool compatibility: Heretic 16/16, DECCP 11/16, ErisForge 9/16, FailSpy 5/16. These counts may reflect failures to abliterate some architectures, such as Falcon-Mamba, but this is unclear from the README.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was read. The paper PDF and result JSONs likely hold the per-model refusal data needed for proper V2 verdicts across tools and models. Re-extract from the paper. The verdict rests on a single unbaselined number.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is measured, projected out at each layer and position, or added.
The README does not identify the tool used for the reported Zephyr result, provide a before-edit refusal baseline, or give refusal results separately for the other models.
No result tests whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
No result compares a single direction with an affine, cone, or multi-direction account.
No result separates harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No result tests transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Although models with different listed alignment methods are included, the README does not test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta
rows.operation_detail: Abliteration weight edit; tool not identified in the README
rows.note: The README says Zephyr-7B-beta achieved this ASR with minimal distribution shift; it does not state the pre-edit ASR or evaluation details.
rows.check: Post-edit ASR only; no pre-edit ASR is given. Zephyr-7B-beta has little safety tuning, so much of the 98% may predate the edit. The tool is not named. The file 'zephyr-7b-beta-abliterated.json' has no tool suffix, which suggests Heretic, but that is inference. The judge and prompt set are not stated.

relationships.reason: r1: 98% ASR after the edit, with KL 0.076. The support is weak because there is no pre-edit baseline and Zephyr is lightly aligned.
relationships.display_finding: The edited, lightly aligned model achieved 98% attack success with KL divergence of 0.076.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: The README reports 98% ASR after abliteration, consistent with strong refusal suppression; see r1. The tool and baseline are not stated.
